substitutes: No spare cloths? Fold one towel in four and use one quarter per leg.
title: The Family Relay Trail
clue: Everyone in the house runs one short leg, and the dog runs the whole race.
reveal: Each person lays one short leg of a scent trail with a cloth or a few crumbs of dinner, and your dog follows the chain from person to person to the finish, where dinner waits. People lay the trail and sit still; the dog does the running.
objective: Lay a relay of short scent trails, one per person, let your dog follow it to the dinner bowl, then share one quiet minute.
instructions: Gather the household and explain the rules as a family: it is the dog's game, and the people's jobs are to lay a leg, sit still and look away. Everyone picks a cloth (a dish towel or scarf) and a start spot. Children never call, grab, hug or chase the dog.
Plan four or five legs on paper, one per person, about ten steps each, finishing where your dog usually eats. Put their dinner bowl at the end in their usual spot.

With your dog waiting elsewhere with an adult or behind a gate, each person lays a leg in turn: drag a clean cloth along the floor for ten steps, or drop a pea-sized crumb of dinner every few steps. Then sit still at the end of the leg, side-on and looking away, cloth in lap.

Release your dog with no cue and let them follow the trail person to person. They may nose a cloth, check a person or skip a leg. People stay still and it is fine if the dog bypasses them. An adult stays close and nobody speaks.
The last person has the finish: a cardboard 'treasure chest' on its side with the dinner bowl inside, open end toward the dog. They stay seated and look away.

Adults sit two meters away looking away from the bowl for one quiet minute while the dog eats, no photos, and children go to another room. Afterwards each person says one thing they noticed their dog do on the trail.
twist: The dog runs the family: they visit each person in order, so who laid which leg becomes the story, with the scent as the baton.
variations: Solo or two-person home: three legs laid by you with three different cloths, finishing at the dinner chest.
Puppy or first trail: one leg, two meters, one crumb at the end, then a long nap.
Scent-map version: draw the planned route on paper first and mark the dog's real route afterwards; it is never quite the same.
Outdoor version: a fully fenced private yard, same legs, with children staying at the trail's end rather than beside it.
completion: Counts when your dog has followed the trail as far as they like, or sniffed a leg and walked away; the quiet minute is the finish either way.
photoIdea: The planned route drawn on paper, or the cloths folded in a row, photographed after the relay, not during.
memoryPrompt: Whose leg did your dog follow best, and what did each person notice?
supplies: A clean cloth per person (dish towels or scarves)
Your dog's dinner ration and bowl
dietNotes: Use your dog's own dinner, split into a few crumbs and the bowl, so nothing extra is added. Ask your vet if your dog has diet limits or an allergy.
safety: An adult supervises: children never call, chase, hug or hold the dog, and nobody approaches while they eat.
Skip the dinner chest and ask your vet if your dog guards food or has ever snapped at anyone.
Use only your dog's usual food, never chocolate, grapes, raisins, xylitol or onion.
